text:
maria_lee: Quick follow-up from the prewarm credits RFC — a few open questions about decay/safety we should nail before the rollout.
ajay: 👍 what specifically?
maria_lee: Two things: 1) avoid mass prewarm storms when many tenants spike, 2) make credits predictable for billing/observability.
kevin_w: For (1) we probably need a global admission soft-limit + per-tenant slow decay. Soft-limit avoids hard rejects.
taylor_ops: Can we implement a gradual backoff on admission rather than outright deny? e.g. reduce admitted warmups by 10-50% depending on headroom.
samir: +1. Also add randomized jitter so we don't sync admit windows across tenants. :seedling:
ajay: Sketching config we could use:
```yaml
prewarm:
  decay_half_life_sec: 7200  # half credits every 2h
  tenant_max_credits: 200
  global_soft_headroom_pct: 12  # try to keep this headroom free
  backoff_scale: 0.25  # scale down admitted prewarms when soft headroom breached
  jitter_pct: 0.15
```
kevin_w: I like half-life instead of fixed leak-rate — fits bursty patterns. But need to reason about corner-case where a tenant comes back after prolonged inactivity: credits should be low, but we may want a one-time grace for prod traffic.
maria_lee: Right — propose a small startup grace token bucket: `startup_grace = min(10, tenant_max_credits * 0.05)` applied once per tenant per 24h.
taylor_ops: How does the operator actually apply backoff? Operator has admission loop with target pool utilization. If util > target+epsilon apply deterministic reduction scaled by `backoff_scale`. Add jitter to the delay before admitting each warmup.
samir: Pseudo admission logic:
```python
if global_headroom_pct < soft_headroom_pct:
    admit = max(0, requested_prewarms * (1 - backoff_scale*(soft_headroom_pct - global_headroom_pct)))
    admit = jitter(admit, jitter_pct)
else:
    admit = requested_prewarms
```
kevin_w: We should also protect against credit gaming: cap `startup_grace` and refuse if tenant previously abused warmups (metrics: prewarm_fail_rate > 5% and high churn).
ajay: Good point. Add a short probation window where suspected-abuse tenants get a smaller grace and slower decay.
maria_lee: Observability: expose `prewarm_admit`, `prewarm_deny`, `credit_balance`, `decay_rate_actual` per tenant and global. Dashboards + alert if prewarm_denies spike > 1% of requests.
taylor_ops: Also instrument operator internal queue length and per-shard admit_latency; useful when backoff leads to queueing.
infra-bot: deploy 1742345700: prewarm-controller v0.8.1 rolled to canary cluster eng-canary (sha: d3f8a2). :rocket:
kevin_w: Can we add an integration test that simulates 500 tenants spiking concurrently and verify admitted prewarms ramp is smoothed?
samir: I can add a chaos test in the sim harness. Will include headroom override to validate soft-limit enforcement.
ajay: One more tradeoff: billing signal. If credits decay slowly, billable prewarm units may be high even when unused. Suggest we record `active_warm_duration` separately and bill only active time + a small reserved charge for cached kv.
maria_lee: Agreed. We'll keep credits for admission only and compute billing from actual GPU-minutes consumed. Credits are admission tokens not dollars. Clarify in docs.
taylor_ops: Implementation notes: operator must maintain a light-weight per-tenant sliding window counter (1m, 1h, 12h) and an expiry to delete idle tenants. Keep memory bounded.
kevin_w: For scaling, shard admission by pool-region and use token-bucket sharding to avoid centralized hot-spot.
samir: I'll prototype the decay algo and sim it against real traffic traces. Expect to share numbers by EOD tomorrow.
maria_lee: Great — action items: Samir prototype + sim, Kevin add telemetry + tests, Ajay update RFC with startup_grace and billing clarification. I'll consolidate and schedule a short follow-up sync. :thumbsup:
ajay: Sounds good.
taylor_ops: If we see emergent oscillation in canary, auto-fallback to a simpler `max-concurrent-prewarms-per-tenant` rule so we don't thrash.
maria_lee: noted. Thanks all.
